gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-deseret: Sturdy and iron-cast, Edo SZ draws its lowercase with the stature of capitals and a single constant stroke width. Noto Sans Deseret reads gently beside it.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-devanagar: Noto Sans Devanagari reads compact and modern, its g keeping an open lower curve. Edo SZ is the showpiece, with no stress in any curve, while Noto Sans Devanagari does the quiet sans-serif work.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-ethiopic: Edo SZ is drawn with no modulation between stems and connecting strokes, so every letter holds one cast-iron stature. Add Noto Sans Ethiopic's tall, sturdy lowercase and you get weight with room.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-lao-loope: Noto Sans Lao Looped sets words as solid blocks, with bowls left unfinished on one side, under Edo SZ's hairline-free display letters. Long reading stays dense and steady.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-lepcha: Approachable and sturdy, this pair starts with Edo SZ. It bends its letters like single wire, while Noto Sans Lepcha keeps curves wide open for reading.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-malayalam: Tubing bent into loops, that is Edo SZ. Its strokes never thin out, and Noto Sans Malayalam adds a dense middle zone with an s that opens generously.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-myanmar: Edo SZ looks like bent loops of tubing, with each n built from matching arch and stem. Noto Sans Myanmar follows as a heavy-looking plain sans strip with a broad c.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-ogham: Contemporary and clean, Edo SZ looks cut from wire in every letter, with strokes that never vary. Noto Sans Ogham backs it with tall bodies and wide gaps in the e, so it looks bold.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-ol-chiki: Contemporary in feel, Edo SZ gives crossbars the same thickness as the stems around them. And Noto Sans Ol Chiki holds its curve tails back, setting words as solid blocks.
gen-dafont-edo-sz-gf-noto-sans-old-hunga: Edo SZ has no thick-thin swing at all, just constant strokes with cast-iron stature. Noto Sans Old Hungarian opens its a, e and s widely, so paragraphs stay easy going.
